findings.finding: Insights: f(n)=min LCM(a,b,c) over distinct a+b+c=n (e.g. 1,2,n‑3 gives LCM=LCM(2,n‑3)). Hence f(n)≤2·⌈(n‑3)/2⌉≈n. Since M≫2025!, (2025!·f(M+c))/M<1 for all given c, each floor=0 ⇒ all g(c)=0. Sum=0/2025! ⇒ p=0,q=1 ⇒ p+q=1. 1 mod 99991 = 1.

Insights: f(n)=min LCM(a,b,c) for distinct a+b+c=n. Minimal LCM equals the smallest possible max c where a,b|c (distinct proper divisors) and a+b=n−c. For huge n≈3^k, c will be tiny (≤~n/3). Compute f(M+c) by finding smallest c satisfying a+b=n−c with a,b|c. Then g(c)=⌊2025!·f(M+c)/M⌋/2025!≈f(M+c)/M·2025! floor. Since M≫f, g(c) is either 0 or 1. Sum six g’s → rational p/q; p+q mod 99991 needed. Pitfall: ensure c values allow f<M/2025! to make floor 0; otherwise 1. Use divisibility of M (3‑power) to test small c.

Insights: M=3^{2025!}. For any c≠0,3∤c we have M≡1 (mod c) ⇒ N=M−1 works (1,c are divisors, sum=c+1). So f(M+c)≤M−1. Need smallest N; check if any N<M−1 works. For c=1 (≡1 mod 3) the above fails; need other construction. Compute f for each given c, then g(c)=⌊2025!·f(M+c)/M⌋/2025!. Since 2025! contains 3^{t} (t≈½·2025!), any N with v₃(N)≥t gives exact N/M; otherwise floor truncates. Sum the six g’s, reduce p/q, output (p+q) mod 99991. Pitfalls: assuming N=M−1 minimal (not always), handling c=0 and c=1 separately, correctly accounting for 3‑adic valuation in floor.

Insights: f(n)=min LCM(a,b,c) for a+b+c=n ⇒ f(n)/n = min {f(d)/d | d|n, d≥6}. Record low ratios: 6/11 (11‑multiples), 4/7 (7‑multiples), 10/17 (17‑multiples), 16/25 (25‑multiples), 30/47, 64/97, 110/167,… M=3^{2025!} ⇒ M≡1 (mod d) for d∤3. For N=M+c (c even) N odd, test divisibility by these d’s via c≡−1 (mod d). Results: g(0)=g(4M)=2/3 (d=9); g(1848374)=16/25 (d=25); g(10162574)=30/47; g(265710644)=64/97; g(44636594)=110/167. Sum = 224414944/57101475, coprime. (p+q) mod 99991 = 41754. Pitfalls: include only odd divisors (N odd), handle d with factor 3 (use M mod d=0), ensure ratios ordered by size.

Insights: f(n)=min LCM(a,b,c)=min L where ∃ distinct proper divisors d,e of L with d+e=n−L. Thus f(n) is the smallest L≥⌈n/3⌉ satisfying that condition. For n=3^k (k≥2) the minimal L is (2/3)n. For n=5·3^k the same holds. For n=3^k+δ (δ small) the value of L depends only on δ and k mod 6; it stabilizes for large k. Compute f for the six arguments (M,5M, M+δ_i) using this rule; g(c)=⌊2025!·f/M⌋/2025! equals f/M rounded down to 1/2025! steps. Sum gives p/q; reduce and output (p+q) mod 99991. Pitfalls: ensure L’s proper‑divisor condition (d,e≠L) and handle δ where L<(2/3)n. Use periodicity in k (mod 6) to get exact f for huge exponent.

Insights: f(N)=min lcm(a,b,c) with a+b+c=N. Minimal ratio lcm/N = min_{k|N} r(k) where r(k)=min lcm for sum k ÷ k. Global min r(k)=6/11 (k multiple of 11). N’s divisors:  
M=3^K (K=2025!): only 3‑powers.  
5M (c=4M): divisors 3‑powers·5 → min r=2/3 → g=5·2/3=10/3.  
Other N=M+c (c small) not ≡0 mod 7,11 → best divisors: 25 (r=16/25), 47 (30/47), 97 (64/97), 167 (110/167).  
Since 2025! is multiple of each divisor, floor gives exact ratios.  
Sum = 2/3+10/3+16/25+30/47+64/97+110/167 = 125561848/19033825.  
p+q mod 99991 = 8687.  

Pitfalls: Include factor N/M for c=4M (multiply ratio by 5); ignore tiny ε from c/M; ensure k divides 2025!.

Insights: f(N) = smallest L≥⌈N/2⌉ with three distinct divisors summing to N. For N≫8, L≤N, so f(N)∈[⌈N/2⌉,N]. Here N=M+c (odd, M=3^{2025!}), so f(N)≈(M+1)/2+O(c). ε=2025!(c+1)/(2M)≪1 ⇒ floor(2025!·f(N)/M)=2025!/2. Hence each g(c)=½, sum=3=3/1, p+q=4, answer 4 mod 99991. Pitfalls: ensure f(N)≥⌈N/2⌉ (true for N>8) and ε<1 (true since M astronomically huge).

Insights: f(n)=min_{S|n} n·r(S) where r(S)=L/S for primitive triples. Minimal r(S) occurs for S≡2 (mod 3) with a=2: r=2/3−4/(3S); for S≡1 (mod 3): r=2/3−2/(3S); S multiple 3 gives r≥2/3.  

M=3^{2025!} ⇒ M≡1 (mod p≠3). For c=0,4M: only 3‑powers divide n ⇒ best S=9 → r=2/3.  

For c=1848374,10162574,265710644,44636594 compute smallest divisor S≥6, S∤3, of n=M+c (use M≡1 mod S). Results: S=25 (r=16/25), S=47 (30/47), S=97 (64/97), S=167 (110/167).  

g(c)=⌊2025!·f(n)/M⌋/2025! = r (since 2025!·r integer; tiny ε from c/M never pushes floor).  

Sum = 2/3+10/3+16/25+30/47+64/97+110/167 = 125561848/19033825.  

(p+q) mod 99991 = 8687.  

Pitfalls: ensure S not multiple of 3, S≥6; r(S) formula valid for S≥11; verify 2025! divisible by each denominator.

Insights: f(n)=min₍a+b+c=n₎LCM(a,b,c). Hence f(N)=N·min_{d|N, d≥6} r(d) where r(d)=f(d)/d. Global minima of r(d) (≤2025) are: 6/11 (11‑mult.), 4/7 (7‑mult.), 16/25 (25‑mult.), 30/47, 64/97, 110/167, 2/3 (9‑mult.).  

M=3^{2025!}≡1 (mod d) for d∤3.  

Check each N=M+c:  

c=0 → N≡0 mod 9 ⇒ r=2/3.  
c=4M → N=5M, still 9|N ⇒ r=2/3.  
c=1848374 → N≡0 (mod 25) only low‑ratio divisor ⇒ r=16/25.  
c=10162574 → N≡0 (mod 47) ⇒ r=30/47.  
c=265710644 → N≡0 (mod 97) ⇒ r=64/97.  
c=44636594 → N≡0 (mod 167) ⇒ r=110/167.  

Sum = 2/3+2/3+16/25+30/47+64/97+110/167 = 224414944/57101475.  

p+q mod 99991 = 41754.  

Pitfalls: ensure 2025!·r(d) integer (d≤2025), ignore even divisors (N odd), verify no smaller‑ratio divisor (check 11,7,25,…).

Insights: f(N)=min lcm(a,b,c) for a+b+c=N. Minimal ratio lcm/N = a/k where k|N, a=min lcm(k). Global min = 6/11 (k multiple of 11). N’s divisors → best k per N.  

Compute N=M+c (M=3^{2025!}). Mod 11 shows none divisible by 11; check small k≤20000.  

Best k:  
M: k=9 → 2/3  
5M: k=9 → 2/3 → g=5·2/3=10/3  
M+1848374: k=25 → 16/25  
M+10162574: k=47 → 30/47  
M+265710644: k=97 → 64/97  
M+44636594: k=167 → 110/167  

Since 2025! divisible by all k, g(c)=a/k (or 5·a/k for 4M).  

Sum = 2/3+10/3+16/25+30/47+64/97+110/167 = 125561848/19033825.  

p+q mod 99991 = 8687.  

Pitfalls: Include factor 5 for c=4M; ensure ε=c/M negligible; verify k divides 2025!.

Insights: f(n)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n ⇒ f(n)/n = min_{d|n, d≥6} r(d), where r(d)=2/3−2/(3d) if d≡1(mod 3), r(d)=2/3−4/(3d) if d≡2(mod 3), r(d)=2/3 for d multiple of 3 (≥9).  

M=3^{2025!} ⇒ M≡1 (mod d) for d∤3.  

For each c: find smallest divisor ≥6 of N=M+c in each residue class; compute r.  

Results:  
g(0)=2/3 (d=9); g(4M)=5·2/3=10/3; g(1848374)=16/25 (d=25); g(10162574)=30/47 (d=47); g(265710644)=64/97 (d=97); g(44636594)=110/167 (d=167).  

Sum = 125561848/19033825 ⇒ (p+q) mod 99991 = **8687**.  

Pitfalls: ignore factor (1+c/M) for c=4M (g(4M)≠2/3) and ensure d≥6, distinct‑divisor condition.

Insights: f(n) = (N_s/s)·n where (N_s,s) is the smallest integer‑sum pair; ratio N_s/s is fixed for each achievable sum s. Minimal ratios (best N) are ordered by s dividing n: 11→6/11, 14→4/7, 17→10/17, 10→3/5, 13→8/13,… For each n=M+c, find the smallest s (in that order) that divides n; then g(c)=⌊2025!·(N_s/s)⌋/2025!. Compute p,q from Σg(c) (six c’s). Pitfalls: ensure s divides n; use M≡1 (mod p) for p≤2025 (p≠3) so n≡c (mod p). Determine divisibility by 11,14,17,10,13,… for each c. Compute sum, reduce fraction, find (p+q) mod 99991.

Insights: f(n)=n·min_{d|n, d≥6} f(d)/d. Minimal ratios r(d)=f(d)/d are 2/3 (d=9), 6/11 (d=11), 4/7 (d=7), 30/47, 16/25, 64/97, 110/167 … For M=3^N, M≡1 (mod 11,7,…). n=M+c divides iff d=3^a·e with e|c+1, e∤3, a≤v₃(c). Compute c’s v₃ and divisors of c+1 → smallest r(d). Results: g(0)=g(4M)=2/3; g(1848374)=16/25; g(10162574)=30/47; g(265710644)=64/97; g(44636594)=110/167. Sum = 224414944/57101475 → p+q≡41754 (mod 99991). Pitfalls: ensure d≤2025! (all are) so floor is exact; handle powers of 3 divisor condition correctly.

Insights: f(n)=min LCM(a,b,c) for a+b+c=n. For n≡1 (mod 3) use (1,(n‑1)/3,2(n‑1)/3) ⇒ f≈2n/3. For n≡0 (mod 3) use (1,d,n‑d‑1) with d max divisor of n‑1 < (n‑1)/2 ⇒ f=n‑d‑1≈(1‑1/p)n where p=smallest odd prime factor of n‑1. Compute d for each n=M,5M,M+1848374,… (M=3^{2025!}). Then g(c)=⌊2025!·f(M+c)/M⌋/2025!. Sum the six g’s, reduce to p/q, output (p+q) mod 99991. Pitfalls: don’t assume sum divisor; use correct triple construction; ensure 2025! divisible by denominators.

Insights: f(N)=N·min_{d|N, d≥6} (minLCM(d)/d). Ratios ordered: 6/11 (11‑multiples), 4/7 (7‑multiples), 10/17 (17‑multiples), 3/5 (10‑multiples), 8/13 (13‑multiples), 14/23 (23‑multiples)… M=3^{2025!}≡1 (mod p≤2025, p≠3). Compute N=M+c mod each small p; find smallest divisor giving lowest ratio.
